setup: Two figures are similar with a length ratio of \([[factor]]\) to 1.

steps.say: Every length in the larger figure is \([[factor]]\) times the corresponding length in the smaller, and every angle is unchanged.
Area has two dimensions, so the length ratio is applied once per dimension: \([[factor]]^2 = [[area_ratio]]\). A volume would scale by the cube for the same reason.

answer: So the larger figure's area is \([[area_ratio]]\) times the smaller's.
